summary: The agent ran the whole six-task plan with hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development in a single turn of about 39 minutes. Both soak tests passed. Each task got an implementer and a reviewer, then a final whole-branch review, a fix pass, a re-review, and `sdd-state finish`, which published its receipt. It stopped twice, both times to ask a question: once at the start (workspace choice and the DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS conflict) and once at the end (how to finish). After my reply "merge back to main locally" it fast-forwarded main. I never had to send "continue".
reasoning: Every criterion is backed by the session log, git state and checksums. The agent kept its turn alive through both long soak tests (240 s and 720 s, run as a tracked job with foreground waits) and never stopped without a question while the plan was unfinished. Its only two stops asked legitimate questions that the script lets me answer.

observations.description: Commits a10f961 and 0d4efbe have the 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Haiku 4.5' trailer stuck in the subject line instead of a separate trailer. The agent noticed this itself, and the fast-forward merge put both commits into main's history.

At the end of the run the agent printed the sdd-state finish receipt path and asked how to finish in the same message. It asked the merge/PR/keep question even though the skill's flow ends in a merge, so the user has to step in at the very end.

The agent said no decision records were written because the decision-record script refuses a spec at the repo root (design.md). It also said the Codex review gate was skipped because the plugin isn't installed. Both are process gaps the agent reported, not failures.

In the final fix pass the agent edited plan.md (it changed Task 5's 1.5 prose to 1.0) and added a test pinning DEFAULT_WINDOW_SECONDS. That's reasonable, but it went slightly beyond 'implement the plan as written', and the user didn't ask for it.

On startup, Claude Code's trust prompt and bypass-permissions prompt both default to 'No, exit'. A model-upgrade prompt ('Currently pinned: Opus 5') also appeared even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I declined it, and the header then showed Opus 5.5.

Untracked __pycache__ directories are left in the main checkout (ratelimit/__pycache__, tests/__pycache__), and the repo has no .gitignore. An extra hyperpowers/state branch is also left behind; the agent explained it is the skill's saved progress for this run.

criteria.criterion: Agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before implementation work
criteria.evidence: Screen: '⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' as the first action. The session log's tool_use list starts with 'Skill hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development', well before 'Agent Implement Task 1: package and clocks'.

criteria.criterion: All tasks completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, work on main checkout
criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use entries: 'Agent Implement Task 1' through 'Agent Review Task 6 (spec + quality)', then 'Agent Final whole-branch code review', 'Agent Scoped re-review of final fix wave', 'Bash Ledger final state, snapshot, finish workspace', then 'Bash Merge ratelimit into main'. Tool result: 'status=finished ... receipt=.../receipts/plan-76cc6a12-20261105T203949Z'. In the workdir, `git log --oneline main` shows 7 new commits ending at 45b9c06 (ratelimit/*.py and tests/test_unit_*.py). Screen: 'I merged ratelimit into main ... main now ends at 45b9c06'.

shasum before the run and after the merge is identical: test_soak_long.py 5cd08cd94378902af0bd11b4ea51618b92265335, test_soak_short.py 5b4fdfd0da5539fa24bacb4c8382355922dcccb3. `git diff c9f88ed main --stat` lists no tests/test_soak_* files.
